findings.desc: quality-duplication: runtime-environment-checks.ts:791-800 (resolveCanonicalCoreRoot) duplicates the exact git-worktree-list-porcelain-parsing loop already implemented in resolveCanonicalSelfCoreRoot at runtime-environment-checks.ts:761-770 (identical 9-line block: split into records, find worktree/branch lines, match branch===refs/heads/main, build candidate=join(worktree,packages,main), return realpath if exists). This copies rather than shares the parsing logic the story explicitly set out to mirror. A future fix to the parsing (CRLF handling, detached-HEAD worktree rows, path separators) would need to land in two places and could silently drift apart since nothing enforces they stay in sync. Recommend extracting a shared helper (e.g. findMainBranchWorktreeRoot(anchorDir): string | null) that both functions call, each applying their own already-different fallback semantics on top.

quality-comment-accuracy: runtime-environment-checks.ts:786 comment ("Any git failure falls back to today's un-canonicalized path") and decision.json preMortem[0].mitigation ("Fall back to the current un-canonicalized corePackageRoot on any git failure (behavior identical to today)") both misdescribe the actual fallback. resolveCanonicalCoreRoot's fallback at runtime-environment-checks.ts:788 is `safeRealpath(coreRoot) ?? resolve(coreRoot)`, which DOES apply realpath (symlink-dereferencing) canonicalization. Pre-fix, this branch used `context.corePackageRoot` directly with zero realpath resolution (see pre-diff line 228: `expected = context.corePackageRoot`), so the fallback is not byte-identical to pre-fix behavior as claimed -- it is a new canonicalization step applied even when git fails. In practice this looks benign or even corrective (it keeps `expected` consistent with `globalRealpath`, which is already realpath'd, so it plausibly fixes a latent false-warn for symlinked corePackageRoot paths that the non-git branch previously had), but the comment/decision text asserting behavioral identity to today is inaccurate and could mislead a future maintainer relying on it while debugging a fallback-path anomaly. Recommend correcting the comment/decision text to describe what the fallback actually does (realpath the coreRoot itself, not a byte-identical carry-over of the pre-fix raw-path behavior).

quality-orphaned-test: packages/main/tests/global-core-realpath.test.mjs (new file, 3 scenarios) is not wired into any executable test surface. It is not referenced by any packages/main/package.json or root package.json script; the root aggregate "test" script (package.json) does not invoke it; "test:all"/"test:legacy" (run-all-smokes.js, packages/main/src/tasks/run-all-smokes.ts:97/123-127) only discovers files matching *-smoke.js under packages/main/dist/tasks, so a tests/*.mjs file is invisible to it; and validate.ts has no generic tests/*.test.mjs discovery. This breaks the established convention in this same directory: the sibling packages/main/tests/milestone-status.test.mjs IS wired via an explicit "test:milestone-status" script (packages/main/package.json) that is itself included in the root aggregate "test" chain. Consequence: this test -- the only automated coverage for the adversarial different-clone-still-warns and non-git-fallback scenarios required by decision.json preMortem 2 -- was run once manually (per the CHK-001 verificationEvidence entries, command: "node packages/main/tests/global-core-realpath.test.mjs") but will not run again on any future regression to resolveCanonicalCoreRoot/resolveCanonicalSelfCoreRoot; "npm test" being green (the checklist's stated acceptance signal) does not actually exercise this file. Recommend adding a package.json script (e.g. test:global-core-realpath) mirroring test:milestone-status and including it in the root aggregate test chain.
